summary: Frontend-only regression + voice-lock verification for the new avatarVoiceLock + ExecutiveAvatar with-audio + auto-unmute changes. All 8 review-request items verified end-to-end with live page evaluations on the production preview URL. Voice lock installs on cinematic / hero variants, neutralizes legacy Web Speech utterances + /tts/speak fetches, preserves __cb_broadcast tagged utterances, and cleanly uninstalls on unmount when refcount drops to 0. Hero now serves avatar-desktop-opt.mp4 (with-audio) and auto-unmutes on first user gesture with localStorage persistence ('cb_avatar_voice_enabled=1'). One regression item (the /portal/ops auth shape) could not be re-verified live because POST /api/ops/me returned 422 with my hand-built `cb_ops_session` payload — but no ErrorBoundary fallback was rendered and the avatar-code path is not implicated.

minor.issue: Returns 422 when a hand-built {email,token} session payload is injected into localStorage (cb_ops_session) — not a regression from this PR but worth noting that founder-access POST returns extra fields (role, scope) that may be required by /ops/me. Recommend documenting the exact session shape /portal/ops expects so test agents can reliably re-auth without UI.

critical_code_review_comments: avatarVoiceLock.js refcount design is correct: install at refcount=1 captures originals; uninstall at refcount=0 restores. Hero (variant=hero) and demo-cinematic both set installVoiceLock:true so dual-mounted avatars share one lock — verified empirically.
BroadcastFeed.jsx line 108 `u.__cb_broadcast = true;` is the critical bypass tag and matches the lock's allow-list check. Don't change one without the other.

Hero variantConfig now sets useAudioClip:true → videoSrc resolves to avatar-desktop-opt.mp4 (with audio) instead of the muted hero-loop. Browser still mounts muted (autoplay policy) and unmutes on first document-level click/touch/keydown via capture+passive+once listeners. localStorage 'cb_avatar_voice_enabled=1' persists the user choice across reloads — verified by reload showing muted=false without a second gesture.

Cinematic demo-cinematic variant inherits the same lock + audio config, ensuring per-scene HeyGen clips (when registered) play with audio while the legacy /tts/speak fetch is rejected fast — the demos' catch{} branches handle the rejection cleanly so scene timers continue to drive progression.

Minor code cleanliness: avatarVoiceLock keeps its module-level state (refcount, originalSpeak, originalFetch) — fine for a singleton pattern but makes it inherently single-bundle. If multiple iframes ever load the app, each would have its own lock, which is the correct behavior.

Note on /api/ops/me 422: not introduced by this PR — but founder-access response now includes role+scope. PortalOpsPage's stored session shape may need both. Worth a small follow-up to make the localStorage shape canonical (one helper that accepts the founder-access response verbatim).

rca of the issue: User-reported voice conflicts (legacy sage TTS playing under silent avatar; homepage avatar silent; audio breaking on scene change) are RESOLVED. Mechanism: (1) avatarVoiceLock module installs a refcounted patch on speechSynthesis.speak that no-ops legacy utterances (preserving __cb_broadcast tagged ones) and on window.fetch that rejects /tts/speak. (2) ExecutiveAvatar's hero + demo-cinematic variants enable installVoiceLock + useAudioClip so the hero/demo plays the with-audio avatar-desktop-opt.mp4. (3) Auto-unmute via document-level once+capture+passive listeners on click/touch/keydown, persisted to localStorage so reload starts unmuted. (4) BroadcastFeed.jsx tags its utterances __cb_broadcast=true so high-signal portal narration still passes. (5) Lock cleans up on unmount via refcount → 0, restoring the original speak (verified: post-cleanup speak.toString() is 'function speak() { [native code] }').
